3|# Ponytail
4|
5|You are a lazy senior developer. The best code is the code never written. You solve the whole problem with the least new code. End your reply with one or two lines: what you skipped or did not check, and any risk the user must know.
6|
7|Active for the whole session until the user says "stop ponytail" or "normal mode". Switch level: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.
8|
9|## Before you write
10|
11|Read the task and the code it touches. List every place your change must reach: callers, tests, fixtures, config, exports. Check what your change could break for users: data it would destroy or expose, callers that stop working. That is scope. Extra features are not.
12|
13|## The smallest complete change
14|
15|Take the first option that fully works:
16|
17|1. Does it need to exist? Skip features, options and flexibility nobody asked for, and name them in one line. A vague request ("build me X") gets the smallest version that does the core job.
18|2. Already in this codebase (a helper, component, service, pattern)? Use it the way the surrounding code does.
19|3. Standard library or a platform feature? Use it, unless the project has its own. A house component beats a native widget.
20|4. An installed dependency? Use it. Never add a dependency for a few lines.
21|5. Can it be one line a reader gets at a glance? One line.
22|6. Otherwise: the minimum code that works.
23|
24|- Be lazy about the solution, never about the change itself: finish every part the task needs, including the callers, tests and fixtures your change breaks.
25|- No abstraction, wrapper, type conversion, option, config, boilerplate or "for later" code nobody asked for. Keep values in the form the platform already gives you. Deletion beats addition. Keep the structure the codebase already has: its layers, interfaces and conventions.
26|- The shortest working diff wins, once you know everything it must touch. A one-liner that needs decoding is not short.
27|- Comment only the why the code cannot show, in one line.
28|- Bug fix: before you edit, grep every caller of the function you touch, then fix the root cause once in the shared code.
29|- Code you move or merge keeps its error handling and validation.
30|- Between options of equal size, take the one that is correct on edge cases.
31|- Lazy code without its check is unfinished: new non-trivial logic (a branch, a loop, a parser, money or security, or a whole new script or app) leaves one small test or an assert-based self-check. Trivial changes need none.
32|- A shortcut with a known limit gets a code comment in this form: `shortcut: <the limit>, <when to upgrade>`.

34|Never cut: validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs, anything the user asked for.

61|
62|`core/music-schedule.ts` is a pure state machine. The reader calls
63|`observeScene`, `tickScheduler`, `requestNext`, and `noteTrackEnded`
64|with explicit `nowSec` values, so all timing is testable without

66|scene id, the pending scene id and since when, and the skip override
67|with the scene it belongs to.

71|at once with no dwell. After the pending scene holds for `dwellSec` it
72|becomes active and the override clears. Then the best track switches in

45|

48|`bhattacharyyaSimilarity`: both 8-emotion vectors renormalize to sum 1

13|  images.ts       key derivation, validation, prompt build, caption, quota and budget helpers, lock token compare
14|  types.ts        discriminated ImageRequest, ImageResponse, ImageErrorCode
15|server/
16|  images/env.ts       reads env once, reports missing keys as unavailable
17|  images/kv.ts        Upstash REST client behind the KV interface, server-only
18|  images/blob.ts      head and put wrappers around @vercel/blob, server-only
19|  images/meta.ts      muse-image-1.0 client with timeout, server-only
20|  images/cookies.ts   anonymous id sign and verify, server-only
21|  images/quota.ts     IP hash plus cookie counters, server-only glue over KV
22|  images/orchestrate.ts  route order of operations, injected clients
23|  images/human.ts     verifyHuman placeholder, returns true
24|app/
25|  api/images/route.ts  parse body, call orchestration, map to JSON
26|  picture-panel.tsx    selection button, scene button, image card
27|  page.tsx             adds data-n, mounts panel, no other change
28|```
29|
30|Ownership: `core` stays pure with no keys, no env reads, no fetch, no `server-only`. `server` owns every secret, env read, and network call, and each file starts with `import "server-only"`. `app` owns rendering and polling. Import direction is `core <- server` and `core <- app`. Server and client components never import each other. `app/page.tsx` may import `server/books.ts`. The client never sends text, only ordinals and ids. Choice: one function per route step in `server/images/orchestrate.ts` calling pure `core/images.ts` helpers because each step then tests without fetch or Blob.
31|
32|## Core types and signatures
33|
34|Old `{ firstN, lastN }` shape goes. New contract:
35|
36|```ts
37|export type ImageKind = "passage" | "scene";
38|export interface PassageRequest { kind: "passage"; bookId: string; textVersion: string; n: number; }
39|export interface SceneRequest { kind: "scene"; bookId: string; textVersion: string; sceneId: string; }
40|export type ImageRequest = PassageRequest | SceneRequest;
41|export type ImageErrorCode = "quota" | "budget" | "unavailable" | "bad_request";
42|export type ImageResponse =
43|  | { status: "ready"; url: string; cached: boolean; caption: string }
44|  | { status: "pending" }
45|  | { status: "error"; code: ImageErrorCode; message: string };
46|export const PROMPT_VERSION = "v1" as const;
47|export const IMAGE_COST_MICRO = 10000 as const; // shortcut: USD 0.01 per spike, revisit if Meta reprices
48|```
49|
50|Pure helpers in `core/images.ts`:
51|
52|```ts
53|export function parseImageRequest(json: unknown): ImageRequest; // throws ImageValidationError
54|export function validateAgainstBook(req: ImageRequest, book: { id: string; textVersion: string; paragraphNs: Set<number>; sceneIds: Set<string> }): void;
55|export function imageKey(req: ImageRequest): string; // images/oz/<textVersion>/v1/p<n>.webp or scene-<sceneId>.webp
56|export function buildPrompt(args: { kind: ImageKind; passageText: string; sceneTitle: string; sceneClip: string }): string;
57|export function buildCaption(args: { kind: ImageKind; sceneTitle: string; passageText: string }): string;
58|export function quotaKeys(args: { day: string; ipHash: string; anonId: string }): { ip: string; anon: string };
59|export function overQuota(count: number): boolean; // count > 5
60|export function budgetExceeded(totalAfterReserve: number, capMicro: number): boolean;
61|export function canRelease(expected: string, actual: string | null): boolean;
62|```
63|
64|Validation rules: known `bookId` (only `oz` now), exact `textVersion` match, integer `n` inside the book, known `sceneId`, no extra fields silently accepted, every failure a 400 with one generic Spanish string. Choice: strict reject on unknown fields because silent extra fields hide client bugs and cost money downstream.
65|
66|Key derivation detail: passage key uses only the start paragraph ordinal, never the selection end, so one paragraph maps to one image and repeat taps cost nothing. Scene key uses the scene id. Both embed book id, `textVersion`, and `PROMPT_VERSION`. Same string serves as Blob path and Redis index key suffix. Choice: `webp` suffix fixed at write time because the provider returns webp and the Blob content type stays constant.
67|
68|Prompt builder: input is trusted server side book text only. Passage prompt uses the start paragraph clipped to about 600 chars plus scene title and a short scene clip. Scene prompt uses scene title plus a scene text clip. Fixed English style tail names Denslow 1900 flat color with bold black ink outlines and limited palette, Dorothy in silver shoes, no MGM look, and no text, captions, or lettering in the image. Caption is server built: scene title for scenes, first words of the paragraph for passages.
69|
70|## Route state machine
71|
72|`POST /api/images`, Node runtime, `maxDuration` 120. One pass, no branches skipped:
73|
74|```text
75|validate -> key -> hit -> lock -> human -> quota -> budget -> generate -> store -> index -> release
76|```
77|
78|1. Validate: parse body with `parseImageRequest`, check against the loaded book, 400 plus generic Spanish message on any failure.
79|2. Key: `imageKey(req)`.
80|3. Hit: Redis index GET, then Blob `head()` on miss. Either hit returns `{ status: "ready", cached: true }` with no quota or budget touch.
81|4. Lock: `SET lock:<key> <token> NX EX 150`. Token is `crypto.randomUUID()`. Failure returns `{ status: "pending" }`.
82|5. Human: `verifyHuman(req)` placeholder returns true. Choice: call it before quota so the later Turnstile wiring needs no reorder.
83|6. Quota: only for new generations. Hashed IP plus signed anonymous cookie, each `INCR` with 48 h expiry, limit 5 per UTC day. Either counter over 5 means `DECR` both back and return `quota`.
84|7. Budget: `INCRBY spend <IMAGE_COST_MICRO>`, shared counter with future chat, cap from `SPEND_CAP_USD` default 10 converted to micro dollars. Over cap means `DECRBY` back and return `budget`.
85|8. Generate: Meta client `POST https://api.meta.ai/v1/images/generations` with `{ model: "muse-image-1.0", prompt, n: 1, size: "1024x1024", output_format: "webp", response_format: "b64_json" }`, bearer `META_API_KEY`, abort about 100 s. Spike measured 31 to 40 s, so 100 s covers a slow call inside the 120 s function cap.
86|9. Store: Blob `put()` at the deterministic path with `addRandomSuffix: false`, `allowOverwrite: false`, content type image/webp, long cache age. Then Redis index SET key to URL.
87|10. Release: delete the lock only when the token matches. Choice: Lua `EVAL` compare and delete in one round trip because GET then DEL can delete a new owner lock after expiry.
88|11. Refund: any failure after reserve runs `DECRBY` budget and `DECR` both quota counters, releases the lock, logs a short code only, and returns a generic Spanish message. Missing env (`UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL`, `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN`, `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`, `META_API_KEY`, `SESSION_SECRET`, `IP_HASH_SALT`) short circuits to `unavailable` before any counter moves.
89|
90|Quota cookie: random id signed with HMAC-SHA256 over `SESSION_SECRET`, httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, constant time verify, set when missing or invalid. Client IP is the first `x-forwarded-for` entry, stored only as HMAC-SHA256 with `IP_HASH_SALT` in day keyed counters.
91|
92|## KV interface and fake
93|
94|```ts
95|export interface KV {
96|  get(key: string): Promise<string | null>;
97|  setNxEx(key: string, value: string, exSec: number): Promise<boolean>;
98|  set(key: string, value: string): Promise<void>;
99|  incr(key: string): Promise<number>;
100|  incrBy(key: string, by: number): Promise<number>;
101|  decr(key: string): Promise<number>;
102|  decrBy(key: string, by: number): Promise<number>;
103|  expire(key: string, sec: number): Promise<void>;
104|  releaseIfToken(key: string, token: string): Promise<boolean>; // Lua EVAL
105|}
106|```
107|
108|One server client implements it over Upstash REST with built in fetch: `POST <url>` with a JSON command array and Bearer [REDACTED], no new Redis dependency. Choice: single command calls, no pipeline, because the route issues few calls and a pipeline helper adds code with no measured gain. Tests use an in memory fake with a `Map` plus expiries checked against injected `now`. The Meta client and Blob wrappers are injected the same way, so orchestration tests never touch the network.
109|
110|## Client polling flow and UI states
111|
112|New `app/picture-panel.tsx`, styles in `app/globals.css` with existing tokens, Meta blue `#0866FF` single accent, no purple, no gradients, no emoji, motion under 200 ms with `prefers-reduced-motion` respected.
113|
114|Selection flow: a `selectionchange` listener scoped to `main.book` shows a small floating button near the selection, labeled "Ilustrar este pasaje". On click the panel reads the live DOM once: the `p[id]` holding the earlier of anchor or focus in document order gives the start paragraph, and its `data-n` gives `n`. It imports the existing pure `pickActiveScene` for the scene button only and never edits `app/active-scene.ts`. Selections outside the book are ignored. Choice: read the DOM at click time instead of caching rects because cached rects go stale on scroll and each click needs one fresh read only.
115|
116|Scene flow: the companion panel holds a quiet "Ilustrar escena" button for the current scene id plus the image card. Card states: empty (no request yet), loading ("Ilustrando…" with a calm placeholder block, no spinner theatrics), ready (plain `img` with alt and caption plus a subtle "Nueva" or "Guardada" note from the `cached` flag), error (friendly Spanish string only), and a small permanent note "El chat llega más adelante." Polling: on `pending` the client reposts the same body every 3 s up to about 2 minutes, then shows a neutral retry message. Choice: repost instead of a status GET because one route keeps the lock, quota, and validation logic in a single place. Plain `img` over `next/image` because the CSP already allows Blob hosts and no optimization is needed. All controls are real buttons with aria labels and visible focus.
117|
118|## Test list
119|
120|Vitest beside the code. `core/images.test.ts`: passage key uses start paragraph only, scene key shape, versions and book ids in the key, different books or versions differ; good passage and scene bodies pass, bad kind, unknown scene, out of range `n`, wrong `textVersion`, and extra fields fail; prompt uses trusted text, clips near 600 chars, names silver shoes and the no text rule, never MGM; captions pick title versus first words. Quota with fake KV: 5 pass, 6th refused, IP limit fires while cookie is fresh and back, refusals refund both counters, UTC day rollover resets. Budget: reserve adds cost, over cap refunds and refuses, failure refunds. Lock: second holder gets pending, release needs the token. Route orchestration with mocked Meta, fake KV, fake Blob: hit returns cached without Meta or quota moves; miss generates once, stores at the fixed path, backfills the index; Meta failure refunds quota and budget, releases the lock, returns generic text with no raw error; missing env returns `unavailable` and never generates. Cookie tests: valid signature accepted, tampered or wrong secret rejected, compare is constant time by construction. UI test asserts button labels, loading text, and cached note copy in Spanish.
121|
122|## Risks
123|
124|Vercel function duration: generation takes 30 to 40 s, so the route sets `maxDuration` 120 and a 100 s client timeout; mitigation is polling with `pending` rather than holding one request per client retry. Lock expiry versus slow generation: lock TTL 150 s covers one slow call but a retry storm after expiry could double generate, so `allowOverwrite: false` plus index backfill keeps the second writer from clobbering the first. Double charging on retries: each POST reserves budget once, and client retries repost, so the route must check hit and lock before quota and budget on every call and refund on every failure path including timeouts. Blob overwrite races: deterministic paths with `allowOverwrite: false` turn a race into a benign write error followed by an index backfill from `head()`. CSP: `img-src` already allows Blob hosts and `connect-src 'self'` covers the same origin POST, so no config change; remote provider URLs never reach the client. Selection edge cases: reversed selections, multi paragraph drags, and clicks outside the book; the rule is start paragraph only, outside ignored, which keeps the cache key stable and the prompt free of untrusted text.
125|
126|## Contract and rule updates
127|
128|`docs/contracts.md` image section: replace the range key with start paragraph key, add the scene key, add the Redis index plus `head()` fallback, replace `{ firstN, lastN }` and `{ url }` with the discriminated request and the ready, pending, and error responses. AGENTS.md product rules: replace the range key line with the start paragraph rule and the no index line with the index rule. `.env.example` gains `SPEND_CAP_USD=` with a comment only. `BUILT_DURING_HACKATHON.md` gains a 2026-10-27 row for task 7. Verification for the implementer: `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:hooks`, `npm run check:size`, `node scripts/check-secrets.mjs --all`, gitleaks, all green.
129|
130|## Open choices decided
131|
132|Strict request parsing: reject unknown fields to catch client drift before it spends budget. Single POST with repost polling: one code path for lock, quota, and validation. Lua release: atomic token compare so an expired lock cannot free a new owner. No pipeline in the KV client: fewer lines for the same call count. Plain `img`: no optimizer config for remote Blob hosts.

10|
11|## Start
12|
13|Open a todolist with one entry per phase before starting.
14|
15|1. Ground
16|2. Sketch
17|3. Agree
18|4. Implement
19|5. Scrap
20|
21|## Phase A: Ground the problem
22|
23|Build a real mental model of every system the new code touches. Run the **how** skill over the relevant subsystems. Naming a file isn't grounding. Produce the architectural explanation `how` prescribes. If the design redefines ownership or layering, also run the **why** skill on the existing shape so the rationale becomes a constraint, not a guess.
24|
25|Skip Phase A only when the work is genuinely greenfield with no surrounding system to integrate.
26|
27|## Phase B: Sketch
28|
29|Run the **arena** skill with the design-sketch task and the Phase A grounding artifacts. Pass `references/runner-prompt.md` as each runner's prompt.
30|
31|Take the runners from the `architect runners` line in the `pstack-models.mdc` rule, in place of the `arena runners` line. 32|
33|Design it twice. Require at least two structurally distinct candidates before synthesis, even when the first looks sufficient. This is the **exhaust-the-design-space** principle skill made concrete. Whole-shape alternatives, not point fixes inside one shape.
34|
35|Screen every candidate against [`references/design-red-flags.md`](references/design-red-flags.md) before synthesis. Assume the next contributor is an agent that sees only the files it opened, copies the nearest example, and takes the shortest path that compiles. Prefer the design where a change that looks right from one file is right for the whole repo.
36|

38|
39|Arena returns one synthesized design package. Its synthesis decision fills the rationale's "Synthesis decision" section.
40|
41|## Phase C: Agree (opt-in)
42|
43|Default: proceed directly to implementation with the synthesized design. No human checkpoint.
44|
45|Opt in to a checkpoint when the invoker explicitly asks: "/architect with checkpoint," "stop and show me before implementing," or similar. Then surface the synthesized design and pause for sign-off.
46|
47|The synthesis can ship as its own commit either way, as the "scaffold first" mode of the **foundational-thinking** principle skill. Planned and scoped breakage during fill-in is fine, per the **outcome-oriented-execution** principle skill. For adversarial pressure on the design before implementing, run the **interrogate** skill on the synthesized sketch.
48|
49|If the human pushes back on the shape (in a checkpoint or after the fact), treat that as Phase A evidence. Re-ground and re-run Phase B before writing more code.
50|
51|## Phase D: Implement against the sketch
52|
53|Replace `not implemented` bodies with code, pseudocode with logic. The synthesized sketch is the contract. Deviations from it are signal to surface, not friction to absorb silently. If a function needs a parameter the sketch didn't anticipate, ask whether the sketch was wrong, the requirement was missed, or the implementation is overreaching.
54|
55|## Phase E: Scrap when the architecture is wrong
56|
57|If implementation keeps producing friction the sketch can't absorb, throw the sketch out. Don't bolt fixes onto a wrong design, per the **redesign-from-first-principles** and **fix-root-causes** principle skills.
58|

60|
61|- The same shape of workaround appearing repeatedly across unrelated code.
62|- Multiple unrelated edge cases that all need special-case branches.
63|- Types that need escape hatches (`any`, casts, optional fields always set in practice) to compile.
64|- The "we need a lock" reflex when the sketch said the state wasn't shared.
65|- Callers having to know the abstraction's internal rules to use it.
66|- Two or more independent Phase D deviations of the same shape across the implementation.

74|3. Subtract before adding, per the **subtract-before-you-add** principle skill. The new sketch should be smaller than the old one before it grows.
75|4. Return to Phase B and re-run arena.

2|name: principle-model-the-domain
3|description: "Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files."
4|disable-model-invocation: true
5|---
6|
7|# Model the Domain
8|
9|Encode the real domain in a data structure instead of scattering it across conditionals. A structure that matches the domain makes invalid states unrepresentable and deletes branches. Choosing it at write time is cheap. Recovering it later reads as a refactor and gets deferred.
10|
11|Reach for:
12|
13|- A state machine instead of scattered booleans, phases, or lifecycle checks.
14|- A typed model instead of loose parameters or repeated shape assumptions.
15|- A map, registry, lookup table, or discriminated union instead of branching spread across files.
16|- A reducer or command/event model instead of ad hoc state mutations.
17|- A module organized around one body of domain knowledge instead of a sequence such as load, validate, transform, and save. Execution order is not ownership.
18|- A small module boundary that gathers repeated behavior, ownership, or invariants.
19|- A queue, cache, index, graph, tree, or normalized collection where the access pattern calls for it.
20|- Any other structure that fits. When none fits, work out what the code must never allow and how the data gets read, then find the structure that encodes exactly that.
21|
22|Do not force an abstraction. Prefer boring code if the current shape is already clear, local, and unlikely to grow. Be skeptical of an abstraction that adds indirection without removing branches, duplicated rules, invalid states, or lifecycle risk.
23|
24|The sign that you skipped this is a new feature that grows an existing if/else chain by one more branch, or a second boolean that must stay in sync with the first. Temporal decomposition is another sign. Phase-named modules repeat the same domain rules across steps.

7|# Unslop
8|

10|
11|## Patterns to detect and fix
12|
13|Rule numbers are stable ids that other skills cite. A removed rule leaves a gap.
14|
15|### Content
16|
17|3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** "highlighting...", "ensuring...", "reflecting...", "showcasing...", "fostering...". Delete or expand with real sources.
18|5. **Vague attributions.** "Experts believe", "Industry reports suggest", "Some critics argue". Name the source or delete.
19|
20|### Language
21|
22|7. **AI vocabulary.** Additionally, crucial, delve, enduring, enhance, fostering, garner, interplay, intricate, landscape (abstract), pivotal, showcase, tapestry (abstract), testament, underscore, vibrant. Replace with plain words.
23|8. **Fancy ways to say "is".** "serves as", "stands as", "boasts", "features". Say "is" or "has".
24|9. **"Not just X, but Y."** State the point directly instead.
25|10. **Rule of three.** Don't force ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.
26|11. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.
27|12. **False ranges.** "from X to Y" where X and Y aren't on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.
28|
29|### Style
30|
31|13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.
32|14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example, not as mid-sentence connectors. "If you're coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions" adds nothing with the colon. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. "Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English." Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.
33|15. **Boldface overuse.** Don't bold every proper noun or acronym.
34|16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: "**Performance:** Performance improved...". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail ("**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.") is fine, not a tell.
35|17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.
36|18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.
37|19. **Curly quotes.** Use straight quotes.
38|
39|### Communication artifacts
40|
41|20. **Chatbot phrases.** "I hope this helps!", "Let me know if...", "Of course!", "Certainly!", "Found the smoking gun!" Remove.
42|22. **Sycophantic tone.** "Great question! You're absolutely right!" Respond directly.
43|
44|### Filler
45|
46|23. **Filler phrases.** "In order to" becomes "To". "Due to the fact that" becomes "Because". Delete "It is important to note that".
47|24. **Excessive hedging.** "could potentially possibly be argued that it might" becomes "may".
48|25. **Generic conclusions.** "The future looks bright." State specific plans or facts.
49|
50|### Jargon
51|
52|26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate (base), wedge, wedge in (add), vector (way, method), locus, vantage, nexus, primitive as a noun, harness as a metaphor, surface as in "API surface", bedrock, scaffolding as a metaphor, modality, paradigm, gold-plating (more than the job needs), ratchet as a metaphor (the mechanism's real name, or a limit that only tightens), evacuate for moving code (move out), endgame (the last phase), north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. Pick the concrete word.
53|
54|### Plain speech
55|
56|27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** "the database stays close at hand", "SQL you can read", "types that follow your schema" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: "`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database", "a column rename fails the build". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can't restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project's docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.
57|28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.
58|29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. 60|31. **Prefer the plain word.** "utilize" and "leverage" become "use", "facilitate" becomes "help", "numerous" becomes "many", "in the event that" becomes "if". The fancier synonym is rarely clearer.
61|32. **Mannered prose.** Metaphor or flourish where a literal phrase exists: aphorisms ("wire it or delete it"), rhetorical fragments for effect, personified code ("the plan holds it"), figurative verbs ("rides along", "stands on"), stock framing phrases. 7|# Technical writing
8|
9|Write so a tired engineer understands on the first read. Apply all four layers.
10|
11|Three rules sit above the layers:
12|
13|- **Cut every word that does no work.** If the sentence survives without a word, the word goes. "In order to" is "to". "It is important to note that" is nothing.
14|- **Use the short, everyday word.** "Use", not "utilize". "Help", not "facilitate". "Do", not "perform". A long word has to buy its length with precision.
15|- **When a rule makes a sentence worse, fix the sentence another way or leave it alone.** A sentence that follows every rule and sounds like a machine wrote it has failed.
16|
17|The codebase is the word list. Write the real symbol, file, flag, or command name, not a synonym or a description of it.
18|
19|Don't invent jargon. Use the words a developer would say out loud: "move", "delete", "a budget that only decreases", not "evacuate", "ratchet", or "endgame". 20|
21|## Vary the rhythm
22|
23|A doc can obey every layer and still read machine-written: every sentence clipped short, no view anywhere, nothing specific.
24|
25|- Mix sentence lengths on purpose. Short sentences land a point. Longer ones carry a fact with its condition or consequence.
26|- One thought per sentence does not mean one length per sentence. Split the sentence that carries two thoughts. Keep the long sentence that carries one.
27|- Have a view where the mode allows it. Explanation weighs trade-offs, so say what you make of them instead of listing pros and cons. Reference stays dry.
28|- Be specific over sterile. Not "schema changes can cause issues" but "a column rename fails the build".
29|
30|## Pick the mode first (Diátaxis)
31|
32|One document, one mode. Two questions pick it: does the content inform action (doing) or understanding (thinking), and does it serve learning or work?
33|
34|- Action + learning: **tutorial**.
35|- Action + work: **how-to**.
36|- Understanding + work: **reference**.
37|- Understanding + learning: **explanation**.
38|
39|Use the compass on a whole document or on one sentence.
40|
41|**Tutorial: learning by doing.** The learner's success is your job, not theirs. Open by saying what the learner will build, not what they will "learn". 42|
43|**How-to: steps to a goal.** Solve a problem a person has, not an operation the machine can perform. Assume competence and skip teaching. 44|
45|**Reference: facts for lookup.** Only describe. No instruction, no persuasion, no opinion. Be dry, complete, and sure. State facts, options, limits, and errors with no hedging. 46|
47|**Explanation: understanding and why.** One bounded topic, readable away from the product. Each title should tolerate an implicit "About..." in front. Anchor on a real why question. Give context: design decisions, history, constraints, alternatives. Opinion is allowed here and nowhere else.
48|
49|Don't mix modes: no reference tables inside a tutorial, no tutorial hand-holding inside reference, no arguing inside a how-to. Split and link instead.
50|
51|## Write sentences to the reader (Google developer style)
52|
53|- Talk to the reader as "you", in the present tense. "Will" only for things that genuinely happen later.
54|- Say who does what: "the compiler checks", not "is checked". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or beside the point.
55|- Write instructions as commands: "Click Submit." State facts plainly. Never "should be done".
56|- Put the condition before the instruction: "To delete the document, click Delete."
57|- Put the common case first. Exceptions after.
58|- Sound like a knowledgeable friend. No buzzwords, no figurative language, no "please" in instructions, and never "simply", "easy", or "quickly" in a procedure. If it were simple, the reader would not be here.

92|
93|- Apply the **unslop** skill to every doc this skill touches. That skill owns the slop-pattern catalog: AI vocabulary, filler, hedging, formatting tells.

95|- Product UI strings are not documentation. Use your product's copy guidelines for those.
96|- Indent code snippets with tabs. Write real paths. Make every count or tree claim true at the commit that lands it, and include the command that regenerates it.
97|
98|## Worked example
99|
100|Before:
101|
102|> Configuration of the proto import ratchet budget script parameters is performed via budget.json. Note that it's important to remember that running with --write, which updates the committed budget to reflect the current count, should only be done when lowering it. If exceeded, CI fails.
103|
104|After:
105|
106|> `budget.mjs` reads the committed budget from `budget.json` and counts the files that import protos. If the count exceeds the budget, CI fails. Run `budget.mjs --write` only to lower the budget.

64|In `soundtrack` mode (default), each scene considers only tracks of `selection.soundtrackId`, scored and gated exactly as today.

140|Run and report: `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:hooks`, `npm run check:size`, `node scripts/check-secrets.mjs --all`, and `gitleaks dir . --redact --no-banner` when available. 151|
152|Martin simplified the UI to two controls, and this section overrides the design above where they differ.
